title: Trade Repository (TR) Data Collections
summary: The Bank of England page describes its Trade Repository data collections under UK EMIR and UK SFTR, which gather transaction-level data on derivatives and securities financing transactions. The data supports financial stability oversight by the FPC, PRC, MPC, and FMIC committees. An April 2026 update modified UK EMIR Validation Rules, setting a reconciliation start date of 28 September 2026.
key_points: Trade Repository data collections cover derivatives (UK EMIR) and securities financing transactions (UK SFTR)
Five derivatives asset classes are reported: interest rates, foreign exchange, commodities, credit default swaps, and equities
Data is reported daily by UK firms and used by FPC, PRC, MPC, and FMIC committees
April 2026 update sets reconciliation start date as 28 September 2026 and removes requirement to reconcile underlying index name field
A revised derivatives reporting regime came into force on 30 September 2024, aligning with CPMI-IOSCO guidance
New UK EMIR reporting requirements came into force on 26 January 2026 following August 2025 policy statement
why_it_matters: This describes the regulatory infrastructure for market transparency. Trade repository data gives authorities visibility into derivatives markets and securities financing, which was identified as a gap following the 2008/9 financial crisis. This is background supervisory infrastructure rather than a market-moving catalyst.
market_structure_context: Trade repositories provide transaction-level transparency to authorities on derivatives and SFT markets, helping them understand market function and counterparty interconnectedness. This is regulatory infrastructure for market oversight rather than a direct market structure mechanism.
